decisions.q: Start building wave 1 (75 tools) once this board is answered?
decisions.rec: Yes. Build the first tool of each new shared engine first (ml-lab, network, security, dance, movement and the rest), then fan out.
decisions.why: Engines built with their first tool keep every later sibling cheaper and consistent.

decisions.q: Deploy the catalog changes (176 new planned tools, 108 code adds on live and planned tools, 8 renames)?
decisions.rec: Yes, right after this board, so a rename you reverse never ships as a dead URL.
decisions.why: Live tools gain standards codes teachers search by, and the catalog shows what is coming.

decisions.q: Should a Native educator review the Native characters and the fishery-management card before build?
decisions.rec: Yes. Ask one reviewer to look at both; build everything else meanwhile and hold only those two scenes.
decisions.why: Authentic portrayal is what makes those scenes usable in classrooms with Native students; holding two scenes costs little.

decisions.tool: Made for Whom?, Voices on the Vote, Missing Voices Archive
decisions.q: Q3. Teach the hard-history topics plainly at grade level (land taken from Native nations, who was kept from voting, whose 1918 records were kept)?
decisions.rec: Yes, plainly and at grade level, with sources on screen.
decisions.why: Teachers need tools that match the C3 standards as written; softened history is harder to teach from.

decisions.q: Q3. Mention child labor in the cocoa chain, or keep only the drought?
decisions.rec: Mention it, factually and briefly, with a dated source (US DOL).
decisions.why: It is the most-taught fact about cocoa; leaving it out makes the tool look incomplete to teachers.

decisions.q: Q5. Add a 6-8 civics and economics course instead of parking those tools in cte-explore and us-hist-8?
decisions.why: Teachers browse by course; tools filed under the wrong course are hard to find.

decisions.q: Q6. Keep K-2 span modules (one tool with a grade switch) rather than splitting into single grades?
decisions.why: One tool with a grade switch serves mixed-grade rooms and saves about 10 builds.

decisions.q: Q7. Keep codes that sit on tools from another subject when that tool does the work (ELA codes on ELD tools, C3 on grocery-run)?
decisions.why: Teachers searching a standard find every tool that teaches it, whatever subject it is filed under.

decisions.q: Q8. Keep the busy modules (5 to 8 codes across a band)?
decisions.why: The codes are honest; each tool still has one idea.

decisions.q: Q9. Its module carries E2-SYS-SE-12, which its spec says it does not teach.
decisions.rec: Add one short activity to the spec that does teach it, so the code stays honest and coverage stays complete.
decisions.why: Fixes the mismatch without reopening a coverage gap.

decisions.q: Q10. Follow the NCAS anchor definitions for MA:Cn10 and Cn11 (the 2021 handout swaps the labels)?
decisions.why: They are the authoritative text; counts are unaffected.

decisions.q: Q11. Take the ELA agent's reshape (almanac editors checking a town record book) to end the clash with misleading-charts?
decisions.why: Two distinct tools are worth more than two that feel alike.

decisions.q: Name the real-world parallel (Gender Shades 2018) in the teacher notes for grade 4?
decisions.why: Gives teachers a real anchor without putting it in front of 9-year-olds.

decisions.q: Keep it about a model's predictions (pothole flags), or make it about generative AI answers?
decisions.rec: Keep predictions as specced; add "fact-check a chatbot" as a separate later tool idea.
decisions.why: Precision and recall are what the standard asks; generative AI deserves its own tool.

decisions.q: Open on Watch (explore first) or straight on Race?
decisions.rec: Open on Watch, Race one tap away.
decisions.why: Students understand the network before they are timed on it.

decisions.q: Team timer off by default, or start at 20 minutes?
decisions.rec: Off by default, 20 minutes one tap away.
decisions.why: Teachers who want urgency can add it; nobody is rushed by surprise.

decisions.q: Who may know a child's password: "your grown-up at home", or add "or your teacher"?
decisions.rec: Say "your grown-up at home or your teacher".
decisions.why: Matches what most schools tell K-2 students, so teachers can use it as is.

decisions.q: Keep birthday on the keep-secret side?
decisions.rec: Keep it, with a line that it is about sharing online, not in class.
decisions.why: Matches Common Sense guidance without clashing with classroom birthday celebrations.

decisions.q: Keep the made-up practice table (labeled), or use a small real public table?
decisions.rec: Keep the made-up table; the class's own data is the real data.
decisions.why: A tiny clean table teaches structure faster; real data comes from the class.

decisions.q: Is the Old Faithful research data set (Azzalini and Bowman 1990) an acceptable source?
decisions.why: Published, citable and famous; its real flaws are the lesson.

decisions.q: Keep all 299 rows (paged), or trim to about 200?
decisions.why: Real data in full is the point.

decisions.q: Claim Old Faithful here rather than for data-desk-distributions?
decisions.why: Distributions already has its own desks.

decisions.q: Frame the unfairness by neighborhood, or name income directly?
decisions.rec: Neighborhood on screen; teacher notes name income.
decisions.why: Keeps a 6-8 discussion calm and still gives teachers the full picture.

decisions.q: Keep the four board and parent portraits, or nameplates only?
decisions.rec: Keep the portraits (already drawn, pending your look).
decisions.why: Faces make a role-play easier to follow.

decisions.q: Name real laws (FERPA, COPPA, California SOPIPA), or a generic state law?
decisions.why: Students meet the names they will see in real policy.

decisions.q: Keep the six portraits, or nameplates with icons?
decisions.rec: Keep the portraits (already drawn, pending your look).
decisions.why: Same reason as the audit board.

decisions.q: Join the perspective family with vanishing-point-studio and city-skyline-studio?
decisions.why: Same camera formula: one engine, consistent behavior, less code.

decisions.q: Approve three generated panelist portraits, or initials only?
decisions.rec: Keep the portraits (already drawn, pending your look).
decisions.why: A panel of faces reads as a real critique.

decisions.q: Add a curator claim naming the race reading of The Gulf Stream, with a museum source?
decisions.rec: Yes, with The Met's own label as the source.
decisions.why: It is the reading museums teach; leaving it out is the bigger risk.

decisions.q: Add a station outside the European-then-American arc (for example West African drumming as a root of American styles)?
decisions.rec: Add the West African drumming station.
decisions.why: Makes the history accurate about where American styles came from.

decisions.q: Gingerbread Boy: keep the classic ending (the fox eats him, told gently)?
decisions.rec: Keep the classic ending, told gently.
decisions.why: It is the version teachers and books use.

decisions.q: Allow the microphone in the tool page's embedded preview?
decisions.rec: Allow it for this tool's page; Plan mode still works with no mic.
decisions.why: Students record without leaving the page.

decisions.q: Share one dancer figure with PE (kit/movement.js, dance builds on it)?
decisions.why: One model to maintain; dance and PE look consistent.

decisions.q: Keep Mayim Mayim, Seven Jumps and Tinikling?
decisions.why: They are the folk dances most US elementary PE and music teachers already know.

decisions.q: Keep the eight styles, or swap one (West African, a Native social dance)?
decisions.rec: Add West African dance as a ninth style.
decisions.why: It is a root of jazz, tap and breaking, so it ties the set together.

decisions.q: Ship with the on-screen disclaimer, or have a dancer from each tradition review the phrases first?
decisions.rec: Ship with the disclaimer; invite review later.
decisions.why: Gets the tool to students; review can refine it.

decisions.q: Add Download GIF (about 10 KB of encoder) so students keep their animation?
decisions.why: Students want to keep and show their own work.

decisions.q: Extend the shared careers.json in place (three Handbook fields the live career-match-quiz ignores)?
decisions.why: One source of career data; the live tool is unaffected.

decisions.q: Career Ready Practices tags: keep 2012 numbers, follow the 2024 list, or drop numbers?
decisions.why: Survives framework renumbering; teachers read names, not numbers.

decisions.q: Keep the unkind group-chat choice at stop 4, or soften it?
decisions.why: It is the realistic choice students face; no slur, no names beyond Dev.

decisions.q: No question box: keep the teacher button that prints blank slips?
decisions.why: Teachers still get anonymous questions, on paper.

decisions.q: Default wording: "Girls and boys" or "Body parts"?
decisions.rec: No default: ask the teacher once on first open and remember it.
decisions.why: Each teacher matches their district's curriculum, which widens adoption.

decisions.q: Periods, erections and wet dreams on by default?
decisions.rec: On by default, with the topic switches on the first screen.
decisions.why: They are the core of puberty lessons; teachers who teach them separately switch them off in one tap.

decisions.q: Add a parent line ("Preview every card at this address; nothing your child does is stored")?
decisions.why: Parent trust is what lets schools use the tool.

decisions.q: Add an opioid overdose scene (recognize, 911, naloxone, CPR)?
decisions.rec: Add it as a seventh scene a teacher can switch off.
decisions.why: Naloxone is now standard in high school health.

decisions.q: Timer on or off by default?
decisions.why: Accuracy first; the race is one tap away.

decisions.q: Take the rename to "Game Day Fuel"?
decisions.why: Clearer and distinct from its neighbors.

decisions.q: Switch to the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines numbers where they differ?
decisions.why: Teachers will be teaching the current edition.

decisions.q: Fictional athletes only, no "my own week"?
decisions.why: Nothing about the student is entered.

decisions.q: Keep the vaping case first, or move it later?
decisions.why: It is the claim students meet most.

decisions.q: Add a "go along" branch?
decisions.rec: Add it, cutting away from the use and showing what happens next.
decisions.why: More realistic, without drawing a student vaping or drinking.

decisions.q: Alcohol scene (The sleepover) on by default for grade 6?
decisions.rec: On by default, with a teacher switch.
decisions.why: Alcohol is in the 6-8 standards.

decisions.q: Add a fifth scene: a ride home with someone who has been drinking?
decisions.why: A classic refusal-skills lesson teachers look for.

decisions.q: Cast drawn in code, or about 11 Codex portraits?
decisions.why: Ships sooner and keeps 11 people images out of review.

decisions.q: Keep 988 in the footer?
decisions.why: A student in crisis should not have to dig for it; resilience-map already does this.

decisions.q: Let students save their starred toolkit on the device (names only, with Clear)?
decisions.why: A toolkit you can come back to is the whole point.

decisions.q: Worry dump: start with an example worry already typed?
decisions.rec: Yes, an example they can clear.
decisions.why: Nobody has to write their own worry to try it.

decisions.q: Default: friendships and dating, or friendships only?
decisions.rec: Friendships and dating, with a teacher switch.
decisions.why: Dating relationships are in the 6-8 standards.

decisions.q: Abusive zone: threats, isolating and control, with no physical or sexual harm. Right line?
decisions.why: Right for 6-8; the Flags glossary still names physical harm.

decisions.q: Show loveisrespect text and phone in the footer?
decisions.why: Same reason as 988: help should be one glance away.

decisions.q: Throwing at the screen: what setup card?
decisions.rec: Suggest a hoop taped to the wall beside the screen as the default setup.
decisions.why: Works with interactive flat panels too; no broken screens.

decisions.q: Session-only log, or allow saving on the device with Clear?
decisions.rec: Allow device saving, this tool only, with Clear.
decisions.why: A month-long goal is what students and PE teachers want; nothing leaves the device.

decisions.q: Show a realistic edited photo (shark in a flooded street) as the hoax?
decisions.why: Realistic fakes are the ones students need practice spotting.

decisions.q: Keep real case names (Oh, Pretty Woman, Ford's memoir, Prince, Google)?
decisions.why: They are the court cases teachers and textbooks cite.

decisions.q: Add a teacher toggle that hides Theo's call and shows only his factor reasons?
decisions.why: Lets a class reach its own call first.

decisions.q: A-SSE.B.3c and A-SSE.B.4 are on the module but not taught. Leave, or place elsewhere?
decisions.rec: Move B.3c to exponent-rule-builder and B.4 to savings-plan (gr 11), which already teach them.
decisions.why: Every claimed code is honest and still covered.

decisions.q: Quadratics left to launch-pad, letter coefficients to model-my-world. OK?
decisions.why: Each tool keeps one idea.

decisions.q: Take "Unit Sense" (applied) or keep "Unit Detective"?
decisions.why: Distinct from the many "detective" tools.

decisions.q: S-ID.A touched only through box plots. Enough?
decisions.why: Keeps the guessing game fast.

decisions.q: Keep the practice-sheet audit for true extraneous roots inside the role play?
decisions.why: A-REI.A.2 asks for extraneous roots, so the audit earns its place.

decisions.q: Annualized withholding, or full IRS Pub 15-T tables?
decisions.rec: Annualized, labeled as an estimate within a few dollars.
decisions.why: Students follow the math; the tables add nothing they would learn.

decisions.q: Keep the "A stops at 26" what-if (A only wins above about 6.58%)?
decisions.rec: Keep it, framed as investing at a long-run stock index average, not savings.
decisions.why: It is the famous lesson, told honestly.

decisions.q: Landlord ending and report wording OK? Teach "medical collections under $500"?
decisions.rec: Wording OK; keep the medical rule with an "as of 2026" note and a build-time recheck.
decisions.why: The rule has shifted since 2025, so a dated line stays true.

decisions.q: Title "Covered: Insurance Claims" (applied) and made-up insurer quotes OK?
decisions.why: Clear topic word; made-up quotes avoid naming real companies.

decisions.q: Military path framed right? Add p25 to the shared careers.json?
decisions.why: p25 pay helps every careers tool show a realistic range.

decisions.q: Add the 9 healthcare roles to the shared careers builder? Parent check for the privacy and oxygen scenes?
decisions.rec: Add the roles; no parent check, a teacher note instead.
decisions.why: More careers everywhere; the scenes are calm and factual.

decisions.q: Small Resume lines mode enough? Keep the optional unsaved "Say it your way" box?
decisions.rec: Enough for now; keep the box.
decisions.why: A full resume tool can come later.

decisions.q: "Startup Booth" OK? $15 to $20 an hour too rosy? Add a valuation line?
decisions.rec: Keep the name; show the hourly figure beside minimum wage; add the valuation line.
decisions.why: Honest comparison and a real finance idea for free.

decisions.q: Keep the 0.30 N tip target? Printer-time limit on by default?
decisions.rec: Keep 0.30 N with a "classroom simplification" note; limit on.
decisions.why: More briefs pass, so students iterate instead of stalling.

decisions.q: Name the Osborne Firefinder in the history line?
decisions.rec: Name it if a USFS source confirms it at build.
decisions.why: A real named instrument makes the history concrete.

decisions.q: Magnetic variation left out. Add one plan with variation?
decisions.rec: Add one optional plan with variation.
decisions.why: Real pilots do it; the optional plan keeps the base simple.

decisions.q: Is the 3x3 color filter enough for A-REI.C.9?
decisions.why: It is a real 3x3 use students can see.

decisions.q: Allow "Download PNG" of the student's rose?
decisions.why: Students keep their own work.

decisions.q: Agree with "Conic Focus Finder" (applied) and the no-cone reshape?
decisions.why: Ends the clash and names the topic.

decisions.q: Add F-IF.B.6 to its module (added in review)?
decisions.why: The tool teaches average rate of change.

decisions.q: Implicit differentiation (AP-CALC.U3) not covered. Leave out, or later?
decisions.rec: Add a short related-rates-and-implicit mode here.
decisions.why: The module claims U3, so the claim becomes honest.

decisions.q: Local linearity and L'Hospital's rule (AP-CALC.U4) not covered. Where?
decisions.rec: Local linearity in zoom-to-the-limit (zoom in, see the line); L'Hospital in hole-hunter.
decisions.why: Each fits a tool's existing idea.

decisions.q: U8 average value and motion on a line not taught. Shell method left out on purpose?
decisions.rec: Add a short accumulation mode here; agree on leaving shells out.
decisions.why: Covers the AP unit honestly in a tool already about accumulation.

decisions.q: Euler's method and logistic models kept, marked BC?
decisions.why: BC students get them, AB students see the label.

decisions.q: F-TF.B.5 and parts of AP-PRECALC.U3 not taught. Narrow the codes? Fake cards OK?
decisions.rec: Narrow the codes to what it teaches; fake cards OK in Race.
decisions.why: Teachers trust standards lists that are accurate.

decisions.q: Keep "Proof Tower" (applied)? Levels in order or all open?
decisions.rec: Keep the name; all levels open, suggested order marked.
decisions.why: Teachers jump to the proof they are teaching.

decisions.q: Use ADA rules as the class standard for home ramps?
decisions.why: A real, documented rule students can look up.

decisions.q: Keep "Slice and Stack" (applied)?
decisions.why: Avoids the mobile game name.

decisions.q: Real can sizes with no brands. Add an invented cereal-style box?
decisions.rec: Keep real cans, no invented box.
decisions.why: Real sizes are the hook.

decisions.q: Trapezoid exclusive or inclusive? Move Frac into kit/curio.js as Curio.Frac? Voice hs-narrator OK?
decisions.rec: Keep exclusive with a one-line note; yes to Curio.Frac; voice OK.
decisions.why: Matches most US geometry texts; one shared exact-fraction class.

decisions.q: Keep the module's S-CP.B codes? Use a real screening example's numbers, credited, disease unnamed?
decisions.rec: Keep the codes; yes to the real numbers.
decisions.why: Real numbers make the paradox land.

decisions.q: Energy-drink study OK for school, or music versus silence?
decisions.rec: Default to music versus silence; offer the energy-drink study as a teacher pick.
decisions.why: No school will object to the default, and teachers who want caffeine have it.

decisions.q: Light themes instead of the dark 9-12 theme?
decisions.why: They are paper documents; paper reads better light.

decisions.q: Show both the test band and the AP (Wald) interval, or only the AP interval?
decisions.rec: Only the AP interval, with a note.
decisions.why: Matches what AP students are graded on.

decisions.q: Board game cafe instead of a casino? Independence test only in help text?
decisions.rec: Cafe yes; add a short independence round.
decisions.why: AP-STAT.U8 needs the independence test in the tool, not in help.

decisions.q: Add a two-way table desk? Recent presidents (Trump 70, Biden 78) fine?
decisions.why: Covers AP U2 properly; ages are plain facts.

decisions.q: Add the two engine additions to the probability family? Briefcases modeled on a TV format, unnamed?
decisions.why: Better engine for every probability tool.

decisions.q: Add a two-hopper mode for sampling distributions of a difference?
decisions.why: AP U5 needs it.

decisions.q: "Town meetings" brief OK? Add an unsaved free-text box?
decisions.rec: Town meetings OK; add an unsaved notes box.
decisions.why: Students jot their pitch without anything being stored.

decisions.q: Company names off screen, towns and ENIAC/UNIVAC named: right line? Keep The Dalles water figures?
decisions.rec: Right line; keep the figures with dated newspaper sources.
decisions.why: Real numbers are the lesson.

decisions.q: Debate claim 8 (real LLMs sample their next words) OK? Keep 60-character typing, never saved?
decisions.why: True, widely documented, and students like typing their own.

decisions.q: Case 1: GPL code in an MIT project, or code with no license?
decisions.why: It is the real-world case developers hit.

decisions.q: Built for one shared laptop. OK?
decisions.why: No network needed.

decisions.q: Made-up board sized like real parts? Add a typed text view?
decisions.rec: Made-up board OK; add a read-only text view generated from the blocks.
decisions.why: Bridges blocks to typed code.

decisions.q: Add t.validate to the shared data-desk engine in this build? Rule-break counts known only after the pull?
decisions.why: Every data-desk tool gains validation.

decisions.q: Add 11 careers to careers.json?
decisions.why: Grows every careers tool.

decisions.q: Safety pauses say "get help" with no phone number. Fine?
decisions.why: No crisis line fits a body-temperature tool.

decisions.q: Share NOAA CO2 with climate-dashboard (seasonal swing here, long-term there)?
decisions.why: Different uses; same trusted source.

decisions.q: Amino acid entry is an atom-only summary, labeled. Keep, or show a real two-step path?
decisions.why: The ledger stays readable.

decisions.q: HS-LS4-2 and LS4-3 rest on the one-trait finch model. Enough?
decisions.why: One trait shows the mechanism cleanly.

decisions.q: Hippo cytochrome c not sequenced. Keep the gap, or swap the species?
decisions.rec: Keep the gap as a real-data lesson.
decisions.why: The whale case keeps its partner.

decisions.q: Budget $4,000k, or a teacher setting?
decisions.rec: Keep $4,000k as the default and add the teacher setting.
decisions.why: Teachers can make it harder.

decisions.q: If the SH 9 crossing figure can't be confirmed, a vague tip?
decisions.why: Never ship an unverified number.

decisions.q: Airway level names cystic fibrosis and F508del. Keep?
decisions.why: Real-world relevance; calm and factual.

decisions.q: Add real micrographs later as an optional view?
decisions.why: Students see the real thing.

decisions.q: Wolves slider capped at 6?
decisions.rec: Cap at 6 with a "real wolves would starve first" note.
decisions.why: Avoids a misleading collapse.

decisions.q: Keep sickle cell disease, hemoglobin C and cystic fibrosis names on the cards?
decisions.why: Students learn why the mutations matter.

decisions.q: Mutations only via protein-factory, or add nondisjunction?
decisions.why: HS-LS3-2 names errors in meiosis.

decisions.q: If the Campbell fly counts can't be checked, use Morgan's original counts?
decisions.why: Primary source, easy to cite.

decisions.q: KCl, MgCl2 and SiO2 boiling points vary. Use PubChem at build and note it?
decisions.why: One named source.

decisions.q: Should equation-balancer, mole-bakery and hand-warmer-lab join the molecules family?
decisions.why: They use the engine; family docs keep them in step.

decisions.q: Only code is HS-PS3-2 (gas laws have no NGSS PE). Fine?
decisions.why: Gas laws are still taught everywhere.

decisions.q: HS-PS1-2 met only through ion charges. Add combustion products?
decisions.why: A staple of chemistry class.

decisions.q: Day 4's 90 percent yeast yield is made up (labeled). Keep?
decisions.why: Percent yield is in the course.

decisions.q: Dissolving framed as "a small bond budget too", with the iron warmer as the true reaction. OK?
decisions.why: Honest and still teaches energy in bonds.

decisions.q: T4 target of 0.50 kJ per gram is made up. Keep, or only compare packs?
decisions.rec: Keep it, labeled as a design goal.
decisions.why: A target gives students something to aim at.

decisions.q: Pairing rate constant with temperature, or show both rates rising?
decisions.why: Avoids teaching a misconception.

decisions.q: Ammonia card qualitative only. Enough for HS-PS1-6?
decisions.why: A numeric mode needs a sourced Kp table.

decisions.q: HS-PS1-2 fits weakly. Keep or move?
decisions.rec: Move it off this tool; equation-balancer already covers it.
decisions.why: Accurate standards lists.

decisions.q: Conductivity bulb thresholds are a model choice. OK?
decisions.why: Labeled as a model.

decisions.q: C-14 half-life: 5,730 (OpenStax) or 5,700 plus or minus 30 (NNDC)?
decisions.rec: 5,730 with a note on the newer value.
decisions.why: Matches textbooks and AP.

decisions.q: Dodge City the only miss. Add a second?
decisions.why: The lesson lands once.

decisions.q: Only HS-LS2-6 taught. Add a climate standard?
decisions.why: Climate tools carry those.

decisions.q: Succession times rounded and labeled approximate. Precise enough?
decisions.why: Labeled honestly.

decisions.q: Keep HS-ESS3-1 (covered only by the people, yields and land panel)?
decisions.why: The panel addresses resources and population.

decisions.q: Feed is a world-scale formula. Enough for HS-LS2-1?
decisions.why: carrying-capacity simulates it.

decisions.q: Energy per person stands in for footprint. Add water or land?
decisions.why: One clear lens.

decisions.q: AEO2023 build costs with 2024 fuel prices, flat 7%. OK, or newer tables?
decisions.rec: OK; update at build if newer EIA tables are out.
decisions.why: Dated and sourced.

decisions.q: Existing coal paid off is the lesson. Add a carbon price slider?
decisions.why: Teachers ask about it; off by default keeps policy optional.

decisions.q: Unserved energy never priced; reliability its own score?
decisions.why: Keeps the trade-off visible.

decisions.q: Take "Up the Watershed" (applied)?
decisions.why: Keeps the topic word.

decisions.q: The $5,000 rain advisory meets the beach goal without cleaning the water. Keep as an option?
decisions.rec: Keep it, scored as "beach goal met, water still dirty".
decisions.why: An honest trade-off students debate.

decisions.q: Costs, flows and loads made up, scaled to EPA guidance. OK?
decisions.why: Labeled as made up.

decisions.q: Challenge 3 saves typed text in localStorage. OK?
decisions.why: Students return to their own design.

decisions.q: Option costs and the room made up. Fine?
decisions.why: Labeled.

decisions.q: Water treatment framed as a simulation with "follow local guidance". Enough?
decisions.why: Uses CDC ratings.

decisions.q: ESS2-1 and ESS2-3 only via Deep Earth cards. OK? Show the 3.42 C lap model beside the IPCC 3 C?
decisions.why: Students see the model and the consensus side by side.

decisions.q: Illustrative rates on the benches OK?
decisions.why: Fair tests still work.

decisions.q: How deep should Futures and the carbon budget go for grade 9? Refresh data yearly or freeze?
decisions.rec: Keep the AR6 ranges; freeze with an "as of" date and refresh yearly by script.
decisions.why: Current data without surprise changes mid-year.

decisions.q: Take "Lake Commons" (applied)? Add a sourced Indigenous fishery-management card, reviewed by a Native educator?
decisions.rec: Take the name; add the card once reviewed.
decisions.why: Real commons management, told right.

decisions.q: Only the Sun and 20 solar masses have sourced later stages. Find a track set (MIST)?
decisions.why: Every mass gets a real story.

decisions.q: Is Rock Clock an honest home for ESS1-5 and ESS1-6?
decisions.why: Radiometric dating fits a time-and-orbits tool.

decisions.q: Lab rules, or a real standard (ASTM F2959)?
decisions.rec: Lab rules, with ASTM F2959 named in Sources.
decisions.why: The standard is paywalled; naming it is honest.

decisions.q: How to frame real health claims? Keep Signal Lab here?
decisions.rec: Sourced claim cards (WHO, FDA) with a teacher note; keep Signal Lab.
decisions.why: Students check claims against named sources.

decisions.q: Keep the 12-particle mode where heat briefly flows backward (with an honesty note)?
decisions.why: Shows the second law is statistical, a real insight.

decisions.q: Sweeping only lowers friction, no curl. OK?
decisions.why: Curl needs physics past the course.

decisions.q: Pokagon's 1895 sentence says "white men" and "red men". Keep with a context note, or drop?
decisions.rec: Keep it with a short context note.
decisions.why: A real primary source in its own words is what research lessons need.

decisions.q: Treat a reference entry written for Curio Class as a citable source?
decisions.rec: Yes, labeled "written for Curio Class" in the citation.
decisions.why: Students practice citing a reference work without copyright trouble.

decisions.q: Use a made-up conservator interview (labeled) and a storyboard with a deliberate wrong date and unhedged "firsts"?
decisions.why: Planted errors are what students learn to catch.

decisions.q: Is Anna Atkins (botanist and photographer) a good fit for "a scientist's life"?
decisions.why: Her life is told very differently across media, and her photos are public domain.

decisions.q: A 1936 radio transcript instead of a "video transcript"?
decisions.why: FDR's fireside chat is public domain and easy to cite.

decisions.q: Let teachers see or change the support/complication tags?
decisions.rec: Teachers can see them; editing later if asked.
decisions.why: Transparency now, without extra build work.

decisions.q: Tycoon currency is hours, not money. Enough of a reshape?
decisions.why: Time is the real research budget.

decisions.q: Keep AASL.Inquire on a grade 12 ELA tool?
decisions.why: School librarians find the tool too.

decisions.q: Add a "my own topic" path?
decisions.why: Students sharpen the question they really have to research.

decisions.q: Native educator review of the made-up tribal fisheries department beside the real Lower Elwha Klallam card?
decisions.rec: Yes, in the same review as computing-team-stories and lake-commons.
decisions.why: One reviewer, three scenes.

decisions.q: Keep C3 D1.5, D3.1 and D3.2 on a library tool?
decisions.why: Social studies teachers search those codes.

decisions.q: Title matches an NEH grant program. Keep, or rename "The Long Argument"?
decisions.why: Avoids confusion with the federal program.

decisions.q: Add a teacher note on the live local debates and composite experts?
decisions.why: Teachers know what to expect before class.

decisions.q: Parent preview for the "who was left out" lines?
decisions.rec: No preview step; a teacher note is enough.
decisions.why: They are standard US history facts.

decisions.q: Several agents ask for a "parent preview" of hard content in classic texts (Owl Creek, Dracula, slavery and boarding schools, Trifles, Equiano, Young Goodman Brown, Du Bois, The Open Window). One rule for all?
decisions.rec: One rule: a short "Content notes" line on the tool page and in teacher notes naming what the texts contain; no separate parent preview step.
decisions.why: Teachers and parents can see it before class, and the texts stay whole as taught.

decisions.q: Bertha Mason note at grade 9: keep or drop? Codex portraits or monograms?
decisions.why: Jane Eyre is read with that context; monograms ship with no people images to review.

decisions.q: Draw its own chart, or join the data-desk engine?
decisions.why: One chart engine to maintain, and the charts look the same everywhere.

decisions.q: Keep Bradford's "wild men" line and Edwards's sermon? Stop at 1929 (public domain line)?
decisions.rec: Keep both with context notes; stop at 1929.
decisions.why: They are the period's own voices; 1929 keeps every text free to show.

decisions.q: Modern Afterlives: show modern titles (title only), or pre-1930 works only?
decisions.why: Students recognize West Side Story and The Lion King; titles alone raise no copyright issue.

decisions.q: Delivery shown visually with no audio, since voice.py uses one style per tool. OK?
decisions.rec: OK for now; add audio when the voice helper supports more than one style.
decisions.why: Ships now, gains sound later.

decisions.q: Keep Trifles here as a guest scene, or give it its own tool?
decisions.why: A one-act play staged three ways fits this tool's idea.

decisions.q: Cut "Indian-fashion" from the Azuela passage, or keep with a note?
decisions.why: Who needed a word explained is the lesson of this tool.

decisions.q: No pins yet for the Middle East, South America or Oceania. Add them?
decisions.rec: Add at least the Middle East and South America (for example the Thousand and One Nights and a Machado de Assis story).
decisions.why: A world atlas with whole regions missing reads as unfinished.

decisions.q: A made-up Suspicion meter labeled "our estimate": OK?
decisions.why: Labeled honestly, and it makes the trade-off visible.

decisions.q: Stockton's "savage blood": teacher note enough, or on screen for students?
decisions.why: Students meet the phrase in the text; context belongs beside it.

decisions.q: Invented closed endings OK?
decisions.why: Comparing closed and open endings is the experiment.

decisions.q: Check the Eisenhower text against GovInfo page images? One paragraph cut from Du Bois and Thoreau: OK?
decisions.rec: Yes, check at build; cuts OK if marked with an ellipsis.
decisions.why: An accurate primary text, honestly abridged.

decisions.q: Spooky Ominous column at grade 10? Audio for the six one-tone versions?
decisions.why: Ominous is mild; one voice style cannot carry six tones.

decisions.q: Review the 23 wave 1 people images (secret-keeper 6, input-or-output 1, design-for-a-friend 3, algorithm-audit 4, data-policy-council 6, gallery-critique 3).
decisions.rec: Approve them as a batch; flag only the ones you want redrawn.
decisions.why: They block nothing until build, and a batch review is fastest.

decisions.q: Kofi's appearance: the spec gives none; the redraw made him a Black teen.
decisions.why: Gives the three friends some variety.

decisions.q: Small green flecks remain on Rivera, Lindqvist and Ana.
decisions.rec: Clean them with a despill touch-up at build.
decisions.why: Cheap, and visible on light backgrounds.

decisions.q: The 105 non-people wave 1 assets are placed, review pending.
decisions.rec: Approve as placed; redraw at build only where they look wrong in place.
decisions.why: Judging art in the built tool is faster and more accurate.

decisions.q: Mary Cassatt, The Child's Bath shows a young child partly undressed for a bath. Keep?
decisions.why: A standard school artwork, used in classrooms nationwide.

decisions.q: The siku (panpipes) has no usable museum photo.
decisions.rec: Draw it with local FLUX (an object, no people).
decisions.why: Every instrument on the map gets a picture.

decisions.q: Wave 2 person image: editor Dr. Mara Quill.
decisions.why: Clean cutout, hands right.

decisions.q: Wave 2 redraw candidates (rmt-sandstone, pc-kraft, courtroom-empty, cafe-after-hours, cts-river-lab).
decisions.rec: Redraw at build only if they look wrong in place.
decisions.why: Same reason as wave 1.
